newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Tuesday due to new issues and listings on the domestic A share markets, which attracted many funds from the repo market, traders said.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 11.95 percent from 11.20 percent on Monday.
Turnover fell to 6.06 million lots from 9.57 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
The A share markets are in a period of record expansion this year thanks to Beijing's support. In Shanghai alone, six new firms will issue and list shares this week.
Traders believe the rates will stay at a high level in the next few trading days.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed after moving in a narrow range and traders said most investors stayed on the sidelines a few days ahead of the issue of the seven-year T-bonds starting on November 1, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell to 123.55 yuan from 123.90.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell slightly to 2.73 million lots from 2.79 million.
